belief: Everyone else has real friends but me.
origins: Social media, church directories, and group photos make it look as if everyone else has a full circle of close friends. Life changes such as moves, marriage, parenting, job changes, and illness can thin out friendships. The longer we are lonely, the more we assume that others never are.
teaches: Solomon observes, “Two are better than one… For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!” Proverbs says, “As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens another.” God knows loneliness: the psalmist prays, “Turn to me and be gracious, for I am lonely and afflicted,” and the author of Hebrews urges, “Let us not neglect meeting together… but let us encourage one another.” Many people feel the same ache. Friendship is built, not found fully formed, and God uses ordinary steps to bring friends.
self_statements: Everyone else has a best friend.
I am the only one who has no one.
I missed the window for making friends.
errors: Comparing my private life with others’ public moments.
Noticing the lack of friends and missing existing connections.
Assuming that everyone else has what I lack.
Predicting that I will always be lonely.
questions: Is it true that everyone else has close friends? How do I know?
Who is a casual acquaintance who could become a friend?
What did my past friendships need to grow?
What stops me from reaching out?
What does Scripture say about loneliness and God’s nearness?
What is one concrete step I can take this week?
truth: Loneliness is common, even when others look connected. Friendships are built over time through small, repeated steps. God sees my loneliness, and He can lead me to friends and use this season for good.
hw_truths: I can take one step this week.
log: Each week, write the step you took and how it went.
actions: Write five people who could become friends.
Ask one person to coffee, a walk, or a meal.
Commit to a group that meets weekly.
Ask God to bring a friend and show you whom to reach out to.
prayer: Father, You know how lonely I feel. Bring friends into my life and give me courage to reach out. Help me be a friend as well as find one. Amen.
hw_questions: Is it true that everyone else has close friends?
What stops me from reaching out?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Two are better than one, so I will take a step toward a friend.”
